Optimal Matrix Chain Multiplication

You are leading a team designing a quantum neural processing unit. Your pipeline involves multiplying a chain of N matrices in a specific sequence. The dimensions of consecutive matrices are given as an array of N+1 values, where matrix i has dimensions dims[i-1] x dims[i].

The cost to multiply two matrices of sizes a×b and b×c is exactly a*b*c scalar multiplications. Different parenthesizations yield different total costs. Find the minimum total multiplication cost for computing the chain product.
explanation: This is the classic Matrix Chain Multiplication DP problem. Define dp[i][j] as the minimum multiplications to compute the product of matrices i to j. Base case: dp[i][i] = 0. For length > 1: dp[i][j] = min over all split points k of (dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + dims[i-1]*dims[k]*dims[j]), where dims is the dimensions array. Fill the table bottom-up by increasing chain lengths. Time complexity: O(N^3). Space: O(N^2).
